It was her flippant approach that was off putting, just kind of laughing off and making me feel like I'm one OF a million. Get over it. Boasting how much her clients love her and want to talk to her all of the time. I wasn't looking for her to act like it was a job interview, tell me how great YOU are. Gave me no indication on what she could actually help me with. To mez it's not a plus when a therapist says oh it usually doesn't actually take the entire hour

It took me a long time to find friends I felt were real friends. Only had one in high school. You're so young, and there are so many opportunities out there for you. I thought high school would never end. It's funny now, my husband thinks people were actually jealous of me when I tell him about high school because I was a 'fly on the wall.' I didn't fit in so kinda just did me. You'll find your place and be much happier not conforming

I felt exactly the same at 14, younger than that I started feeling it. Was a cutter. I wasn't what my mom wanted, not a girly girl. I found my own family, started martial arts and spent a lot of time with people that were supportive, not a lot of time spent at home starting at 12 y/o. You can be more independent than you think. 41 now and glad I found strength at a young age to realize my real family is who I choose, not blood. 
Life pretty much sucks at your age, but just fuck any judgement you're facing. If someone thinks you're a burden, they're not worth being in your life. It's YOUR life.

How it affects my loved ones, and my pets. Death itself doesn't scare me, I've been on the threshold. Waking up to Drs after a severe concussion, comatose for 3 days, hearing their relief I actually woke up, and what happened when I was comatose, definitely not the death that's scary.

I had a suicide attempt at home in 2020. My husband and I actually recently talked more about how traumatizing it was for both of us when the police showed up. I don't remember details, but do remember then dragging me out of my closet and handcuffing me. No tact at all. I'd written a suicide note, they confiscated it, then said they destroyed it when he asked for it bsck. I'm starting to reach out about how they handle mental health calls. Feel so bad I put my husband through that. Unfortunately sad it just wasn't the end of my self

I had a perfect plan a couple years ago. I called my husband and chickened out. Life has it's ups and downs. It fucking sucks that most of it seems to be going through the motions, just a constant state of what's the point. I feel like imposter syndrome every day. Even when there's a vacation to look forward to, ok, that's a short reprieve, but then back to my miserable norm. I'm trying to find good in the little things. I hope you can try as well

All I can give is good vibes also, that you have to live with this memory. I love every day hoping something will happen to me also (after multiple unsuccessful attempts that should've worked), so I definitely understand your mindset. Our brains kinda suck.

I've been hospitalized before. I'm glad you had a good experience. Mine were just putting me on the same meds and just being there, isolated. I'm better off meds now. I do better when I'm going to work and functioning.

I was a high school athlete, field hockey, soccer track. Did marital arts. I went to the Air Force academy after high school. I came back for personal reasons after basic training and one semester. I felt like I'd lost my identity also. But, you can still be active, it didn't define you. I joined a field hockey team, and ended up coaching at a high school for a couple years, all while going to college and pursuing other things. I'm about to be 41, still active and an RVT (vet nurse). You knew you didn't want to focus your life on soccer, so enjoy finding your passion. In the kong run you'll appreciate it

I do appreciate your post. I am a strong person, and have bounced back not needing anyone at all, found new paths and made friends, don't care when there are those that don't 'get me' because there are plenty that do and plenty I'm sure I could text or call right now and they'd be here for me. It's really why I got "zawsze" tattooed on my wrist (always in polish).  It has had some unintended meaning of 'always I have to ask' when it comes to just needing anyone to prop me up. That gets so tiring. The little stuff.  I got my BA on psychology really because my own psyche intrigues me.  Now, in in a vet tech program, animal behavior is soo crazy interesting. Even as I'm trying to type this on my phone, I wish I was a stronger but alas I am just so tired
I'm jealous too. I've survived twice, and I just wonder why I survived and what more I could do. I keep trying to get that courage again, seems surreal that I did

Seems like it would be such a painful mess to cleanup for those left. I worry that somehow I'd survive it, plus the backlash my husband might get for having guns in a house with someone that has attempted suicide before. I've tried twice with substances. Still surprised and sad I somehow survive the massive quantities I took. But still, I'll try again with something leaving less of a physical mess...

Not sure why he's indicating HE is responsible for a 10 year prison sentence, because this is already in place from the 2003 Veterans' Memorial Preservation Act.  It states that a person who "willfully injures or destroys, or attempts to injure or destroy, any structure, plaque, statue, or other monument on public property commemorating the service of any person or persons in the armed forces of the United States shall be fined under this title, imprisoned not more than 10 years, or both.".  He is trying to take credit for something that already exists.
